title: Mixed power-mean comparison
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $0<q\le p$ be real numbers, and let $F:\{0,1\}^n\times\{0,1\}\to\mathbb R$ be nonnegative. Taking all means with respect to the uniform measures on the indicated cubes, one has $M_q\bigl(x\mapsto M_p(y\mapsto F(x,y))\bigr)\ge M_p\bigl(y\mapsto M_q(x\mapsto F(x,y))\bigr)$, where the inner means use the one-dimensional cube and the outer means use the $n$-dimensional cube.
hypotheses_covered: $F$ is nonnegative at every pair of cube points
replaced: Let $0<q\le p$ and $F:\{0,1\}^n\times\{0,1\}\to[0,\infty)$. Writing $M_{r,z}u=(\E_z u^r)^{1/r}$ for uniform means, $M_{q,x}(M_{p,b}F(x,b))\ge M_{p,b}(M_{q,x}F(x,b))$.
